transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Luma Head of AI), Elena Garcia (Luma Director of Product), Marcus Li (Luma SRE), Sofia Martinez (Luma Finance)
Recording ID: m-2025-07-22-luma-capstone-001

Summary:
This is the capstone sync for the 5-week pilot. Review of performance, cost, and readiness for handoff + procurement. Focus on final success criteria, small tuning items, and a business-case summary for finance. Customer leaning toward Dedicated but needs final econ numbers and legal timeframe.

Topics:
- Performance recap (latency, throughput, quality)
- Cost profile and optimization levers (batching, quant profiles, KV caching)
- Security / VPC access and audit logs
- Final success criteria & stakeholder sign-off path
- Next steps for procurement and exec readout

[00:00] Jordan Hayes: All right, folks, thanks for joining. Quick round — I think we have everybody listed, I'll call the meeting to order. How's everyone doing?
[00:14] Raj Patel: Good, good. Thanks. Busy week but excited to see the numbers.
[00:20] Elena Garcia: Hi all, ready to get through this. Want to make sure product and finance lines up.
[00:27] Marcus Li: Marcus joining — SRE. I have a couple infra notes at the end.
[00:32] Sofia Martinez: Sofia here, finance — looking mostly at unit economics and procurement timeline.
[00:40] Maya Chen: Hey, Maya from Redwood, I'll run through the tech scorecard and the tuning notes.

[02:05] Jordan Hayes: Cool. Quick agenda — Maya will do performance + tuning, I'll run the business case, then open for Q&A and confirm next steps. If anything missing call it out now.
[02:20] Elena Garcia: Add compliance questions — SOC2/ISO and logs.

[04:10] Maya Chen: Okay, performance recap. Over the pilot we ran the Luma summarization model using the 13B open model variant. Baseline latency median was about 260ms for 512 tokens, p95 about 580ms on Redwood Dedicated small pool. We tried three quant profiles. With int8 quant plus KV prefix caching we saw median drop to ~190ms and p95 to 420ms. Throughput at 8 concurrent streams average was 72 reqs/sec.
[04:45] Raj Patel: Wait — are those numbers for hosted or dedicated? I thought we had dedicated nodes for the pilot.
[04:52] Maya Chen: Yes, dedicated. These were from the dedicated pool with reserved GPUs. Hosted would be similar but had slightly higher variance; the thing to note is caching had the largest impact for your workload because many requests shared prefixes.
[05:30] Jordan Hayes: And cost? Elena, Marcus and Sofia will want to see the delta.
[05:36] Maya Chen: Right. On per-1M tokens, baseline (no quant, no cache) came to ~ $420. With quant+cache it moved to ~ $260 per 1M. The detailed spreadsheet is in the shared artifacts (see benchmark sheet link). Apologies if the auto transcript munged the sheet name — it is redwood.net/bench/luma_week5.csv (we'll put a clean link).
[06:20] Sofia Martinez: So that's ~38% savings with the optimizations? Good. What's the cost to move to the Dedicated reserved block versus pay-as-you-go?
[06:32] Jordan Hayes: We'll include that in the cost model but rough numbers: a 12-month reserved commit for your expected baseline load looks like ~15% additional savings beyond the optimized per-token rate because of reserved capacity. We'll show both monthly/annual.

[08:01] Elena Garcia: On quality, any regression from quant? Some hallucination checks we ran earlier showed slight edge cases.
[08:10] Maya Chen: We ran the prompt set of 120 critical prompts. Average ROUGE/semantic similarity dropped by 0.6 points with int8 on the 13B; most differences were edge cases where tokenization and math operations in the prompts changed. For the top-25 product prompts, human evals didn't flag major regressions; we recommend keeping int8 for non-math flows and switching to unquantized for the handful of prompts.
[09:00] Raj Patel: Is dynamic routing an option? If a prompt looks like it needs higher fidelity route it to unquantized path?
[09:08] Maya Chen: Yes, smart routing supports that — policy-based fallback. You can route by prompt tags, latency budget, or feature flags. We can demo a rule-based snippet.

[11:23] Marcus Li: On infra, we tested VPC peering. The peering worked but we saw a packet loss spike during our longer runs — seems like MTU mismatch in the testing account. Marcus continues: I'll need a test account with a slightly different network path to validate.
[11:45] Jordan Hayes: Noted — Marcus, action item to confirm peering specifics and send us the logs.

[13:10] Maya Chen: Quick note on caching — prefix caching needs consistent prompt templates. If product moves to dynamic prompt assembly, cache hit rate drops. The pilot had a 62% cache hit rate which is what gave you the big cost wins.
[13:40] Elena Garcia: We can standardize templates for the 40 top flows. Will need a doc for engineers.

[15:00] Jordan Hayes: Moving to the business case — I have a 12-month projection in the deck. Baseline we used your actual pilot traffic shape scaled to projected MAU growth. Net savings with optimizations and a dedicated commit results in a payback of about 6 months versus our conservative internal on-prem estimate. The key assumptions are: 1) 62% cache hit, 2) steady prompt length 400-600 tokens, 3) 90% of flows served by quantized model.
[16:10] Sofia Martinez: Can you send version with conservative and aggressive scenarios? Need one for procurement and one for exec.
[16:20] Jordan Hayes: Yes — we'll send conservative, base, and aggressive slides + a raw CSV.

[18:00] Raj Patel: We also discussed compliance — audit logs, SSO, KMS. Are those all in Private? We need KMS integration and retention policies for logs for 2 years.
[18:12] Maya Chen: Private deployment (VPC) supports customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and retention. Hosted can do encrypted logs and KMS integration but for complete isolation and your retention needs we recommend Redwood Private. We'll share a SOC2 artifacts packet and the KMS integration guide.

[20:05] Elena Garcia: Our legal wants to review data flows. Can you send an architecture diagram with PII controls annotated?
[20:14] Jordan Hayes: Yep — Maya, action — add diagram to the shared folder with PII redaction notes.

[22:30] Maya Chen: Tuning notes — we recommend: 1) keep int8 for summary flows, 2) mark arithmetic/math prompts for unquantized route, 3) tighten template standardization, 4) increase cache TTL to 2 hours for the top flows. We'll push a patch to your staging cluster for one hour to validate.
[23:05] Marcus Li: When you say patch to staging, do you need credentials? We prefer short-lived tokens.
[23:12] Maya Chen: Yes, short-lived service account tokens — we'll take those. We also support ephemeral SSH jumpbox access if needed.

[25:00] Jordan Hayes: Let's circle on sign-off criteria. Raj, Elena — what does success look like for you?
[25:10] Raj Patel: For AI: latency p95 < 500ms for typical flows, cost per 1M tokens < $300 on committed load, and no >2% accuracy regression on critical prompts.
[25:30] Elena Garcia: Product wants operational readiness: runbook, rollback plan, rate-limit policy, and a way to annotate prompts for routing.
[25:45] Sofia Martinez: Finance wants a procurement window and invoice terms — we prefer Net30 and an annual commit if the savings are as projected.

[27:00] Jordan Hayes: Good — those are actionable. We'll put all of that into the sign-off doc.

[28:12] Raj Patel: A couple of blockers: 1) legal review timeline (they're on PTO next week), 2) SRE wants a dry-run of VPC peering on a mirrored network.
[28:28] Marcus Li: Correct — I can do the mirrored network test but need the peering account.

[29:40] Maya Chen: For the dry-run we'll spin a canary with 5% traffic and automatic fallback to hosted if latency goes over threshold. We can provide the canary policy.

[31:02] Elena Garcia: One more question — any vendor lock-in if we adopt Redwood Private? Our architects worry about portability.
[31:15] Jordan Hayes: No vendor lock-in per se — models and prompts are yours, and we can export KV caches and model weights you supply. The platform is opinionated on routing and runtime but we provide export hooks. We'll document the escape hatch.

[33:10] Sofia Martinez: On procurement — is there a minimum commitment for Dedicated? Asking because procurement needs clarity.
[33:18] Jordan Hayes: The committed reserved pool we quoted is 3 months minimum for the pilot conversion, standard enterprise term is 12 months for best pricing. We'll put both options in the pricing sheet.

[35:50] Raj Patel: Any competitors we should watch? We ran a quick bench with Vertex and saw lower cost on some long-tail workloads but with higher variance. Anthropic looked attractive for safety controls.
[36:05] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll include a short comparison slide with the bench caveats — comparing latency variance, tooling, and observability.

[37:40] Jordan Hayes: OK let's confirm action items (I'll read them). Jordan: send annotated benchmark CSV + slides. Maya: canary playbook + runbook edits + architecture diagram with PII flags. Marcus: VPC peering test and logs. Raj: finalize acceptance criteria and compliance checklist. Sofia: procurement contact + PO timeline. Anyone disagree?
[38:05] Elena Garcia: Sounds right.
[38:12] Raj Patel: Agree.

[39:30] Maya Chen: Quick note — the caching change requires template stability; if you reassemble prompts on the fly we'll lose hits. We'll provide a short engineer-facing doc.
[40:00] Marcus Li: I'll coordinate with your eng team for the test account.

[41:45] Jordan Hayes: Timeline — we'll deliver the cost model and annotated bench by Friday (2025-07-25). Maya will publish the canary playbook by Sunday night and we'll schedule the exec readout tentatively for 2025-07-29 or 30.
[42:10] Sofia Martinez: That works. Procurement will aim for a PO before end of August if the numbers hold.

[44:00] Elena Garcia: A very small nit — can you add our SLO names to the dashboard? We have internal labels.
[44:08] Maya Chen: Yep — we can add custom SLO tags.

[45:50] Jordan Hayes: Any final questions?
[46:00] Raj Patel: No more from me. Quick thanks to the team, this was helpful.
[46:12] Elena Garcia: Thanks.
[46:20] Marcus Li: Thanks, talk soon.
[46:25] Sofia Martinez: Bye.

Recap / Close:
- Redwood to send final bench + cost scenarios (conservative/base/aggressive) and an annotated CSV by 2025-07-25.
- SE to produce canary rollout playbook + runbook and architecture diagram with PII notes by 2025-07-27.
- Customer to confirm sign-off success criteria and procurement timeline by 2025-07-29.
- Infrastructure check: Marcus to validate VPC peering and provide logs by 2025-07-24.

Artifacts referenced:
- redwood.net/bench/luma_week5.csv (final link to be provided by Jordan)
- deck: Luma Pilot Capstone — 2025-07-22 (attached in meeting invite)

End of transcript.
